name: Pajak Penghasilan Pasal 21 (income tax withholding)
authority: PP 58/2023 and PMK 168/2023, in force 1 January 2024 — for every tax period but the last, a permanent employee's withholding is the monthly average effective rate (tarif efektif rata-rata, TER) for the employee's PTKP category applied to monthly gross. Category A is PTKP TK/0 (54,000,000) and TK/1 & K/0 (58,500,000), 44 brackets; category B is TK/2 & K/1 (63,000,000) and TK/3 & K/2 (67,500,000), 40 brackets; category C is K/3 (72,000,000), 41 brackets — all transcribed from the PMK 168/2023 Lampiran. Employee JHT (2%) and JP (1%) are charged as their own schemes and are not read as a relief on this scheme’s base: PMK 168/2023 art.15 applies the TER to gross. The last tax period is the first rung: the annual UU PPh art.17(1)(a) progression on PKP = year gross − biaya jabatan (5%, at most 6,000,000; PMK 250/PMK.03/2008) − the year's employee JP and JHT (PMK 168/2023 art.10(3)(b), iuran terkait program pensiun dan hari tua kepada BPJS Ketenagakerjaan) − PTKP, PKP rounded down to the whole thousand (UU PPh art.17(4)), less the year's withholding, a negative charge being the refund. Employer-borne JKK, JKM and the 4% Kesehatan are additions to the taxable gross (`produced.<code>.employer` in `assessed_on`). Applied 2026-09-18: employer-borne JKK, JKM and BPJS Kesehatan premiums are additions to the gross (PMK 168/2023 art.5(1)); in the five labour-intensive sectors an employee with a monthly gross up to 10,000,000 has the PPh 21 borne by the government for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods (PMK 10/2025, PMK 105/2025; entity fact `pph21_dtp_sector`), so nothing is withheld from them. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): UU 36/2008 art.7(1): the PTKP dependant count is the dependants in a direct line of blood or marriage and adopted children, at most three (`employee.dependents_count`, capped), not the children on record; the `ptkp` election KI is PMK 168/2023 art.9(3): a married woman who shows the local government's written statement that her husband has no income is given PTKP for herself, the married status and her dependants — never the spouse's own 54,000,000, which UU 36/2008 art.7(1) grants only in a combined annual return, not in withholding (corrected 2026-09-23); PMK 168/2023 art.10(2): biaya jabatan is 5% to Rp 500,000 a month, so the year’s cap is 500,000 for each month employed (`year.months_employed`); PMK 10/2025 art.2: the Government-borne PPh 21 is for a gross fixed and regular income of at most Rp 10,000,000 in the month (`BASE` and the fixed allowances), not the whole taxable base; PP 68/2009: severance (pesangon, UPMK) is taxed at its own final rates and is outside the TER base; a non-resident is under PPh 26. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): UU 36/2008 art.21(5a) as amended by UU 7/2021 (HPP): the withholding rate for a taxpayer without an NPWP is 20% higher than for one who shows it — every rung, the year-end reckoning included, is multiplied by 1.2 under the PPH21 election `no_tax_id`. Since UU KUP art.2(1a) as amended by UU 7/2021 a resident’s NIK serves as the NPWP and DJP PENG-6/PJ.09/2024 applies no surcharge where a valid NIK is given, so the election is for a recipient with neither. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 3): PMK 168/2023 art.9(4) — the PTKP (and so the TER category and the December reckoning) is the status at the start of the calendar year. The PPH21 elections `ptkp_marital_status`, `ptkp_dependants` and `ptkp` are dated declarations whose later changes apply from the next 1 January (`change_effect` YEAR_START); unrecorded, the employee's current marital status and dependants count are read. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): tax residence (UU PPh art.2(3)–(4)), the PTKP status and dependants at 1 January (art.7(2)), the tax identity (art.21(5a)) and, for a married employee, the gender are declared inputs; an unknown one stops the calculation rather than taking the resident, favourable or current-record reading.

elections.label: PTKP tax status
elections.description: PMK 168/2023 art.9(3): `KI` where a married woman employee shows the local government’s written statement that her husband has no income, so her PTKP includes the spouse and dependants. Unrecorded is no such statement: a married woman’s PTKP is her own.

elections.label: PTKP marital status on 1 January
elections.description: UU PPh art.7(2); PMK 168/2023 art.9(4): the PTKP is the status at the start of the calendar year (for a person arriving to reside in Indonesia, the start of the arrival month). A later change applies from the next 1 January. A resident employee’s status is declared, never read from the current family record.

elections.label: PTKP dependants on 1 January
elections.description: UU PPh art.7(1)(c), (2): family by blood or marriage in a direct line and adopted children, wholly supported, at most three, counted at the start of the year. Declared by the employee; the household record does not establish it.

elections.label: No NPWP and no NIK usable as NPWP
elections.description: UU PPh art.21(5a): an employee without an NPWP is withheld at a rate 20% higher. A resident’s NIK serves as the NPWP once validated (UU KUP art.2(1a) as amended by UU 7/2021; PMK 112/2022; DJP PENG-6/PJ.09/2024), so the surcharge applies only where neither is held. Declared for every resident employee; there is no default.

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Kecelakaan Kerja (work accident)
authority: PP 44/2015 Pasal 16(1): JKK by risk group — I 0.24%, II 0.54%, III 0.89%, IV 1.27%, V 1.74% of the wage, employer-borne. PP 37/2021 Pasal 11 as amended by PP 6/2025 funds JKP by recomposing 0.14% out of this rate; the employer is billed the full JKK rate and no separate JKP line (BPJS Ketenagakerjaan billing, and the seeded company's own listing). PP 44/2015 art.16(1) — an employer-only premium banded by the employer's registered work-risk group, in five groups from sangat rendah to sangat tinggi. PP 49/2023 art.16A, in force 6 October 2023, recomposes every rate by 0.14 percentage points into JKP for a wage earner required and registered in the JKP programme, giving 0.10 / 0.40 / 0.75 / 1.13 / 1.60; the art.16(1) rates 0.24 / 0.54 / 0.89 / 1.27 / 1.74 survive only for the art.16A(3) population, which this version does not model. name: BPJS Kesehatan (health insurance)
authority: Perpres 82/2018 art.30 as amended — 5% of the monthly wage, 1% from the employee and 4% from the employer, charged on wage between a floor and a ceiling (Perpres 59/2024 art.32(1) and (2) — the third amendment, in force 8 May 2024 — restating the ceiling and floor; art.31 was deleted by Perpres 64/2020 and art.30(2) is the direct-payment rule). The floor art.32(2) states is the workplace UMK, with the UMP only as the art.32(3) fallback; Applied 2026-09-18: `by_region` carries the Kabupaten Bekasi UMK (Kepgub Jabar 2026) beside the UMP, and the company’s region names it, so the floor is the workplace UMK. SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AP5` = 1% (employee) and `!AU5` = 4% (employer); `!AG5` prints the combined 5%. The 12,000,000 ceiling is read off two employees — see ID_BPJS_CEILINGS_OBSERVED. name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Kehilangan Pekerjaan (job loss)
authority: PP 37/2021 Pasal 11 as amended by PP 6/2025: the JKP contribution is 0.36% of the wage capped at Rp5,000,000 (Pasal 11(7)–(8)), of which 0.22% is the central government's and 0.14% is recomposed out of the JKK contribution the employer already pays; nothing is charged on a payslip beyond JKK. PP 37/2021 art.43 as amended by PP 6/2025 art.11, in force 7 February 2025 — 0.36% of the monthly wage, of which 0.22% is borne by the Central Government and 0.14% comes from recomposing JKK (PP 49/2023 art.16A). Only that recomposed 0.14% is an employer charge: JKK class III 0.75 + JKM 0.30 + JKP 0.14 = 1.19% of wage, the same total the source workbook's 0.89 + 0.30 charges; only the composition of the payslip lines moves. JKP is open to Indonesian nationals under 54 whose employer is not in contribution arrears (the rule `when`; a NOT_REGISTERED fact for arrears). Neither nationality nor JKP registration is a `rate_selector` axis; both belong on employment_statutory_facts. Applied 2026-09-18: PP 37/2021 art.4 covers an Indonesian national under 54 (`citizenship`, `age`); a NOT_REGISTERED fact takes an employment out where the employer is not current. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750.

rules.when: !(person.employee.citizenship in ["CITIZEN", "FOREIGNER"])
rules.refusal: Record the employee as an Indonesian citizen or a foreign national on the employment terms: BPJS participation of a foreign worker turns on six months’ work in Indonesia (UU 24/2011 art.14; PP 44/2015 art.1 angka 4; Perpres 82/2018 art.1 angka 2) and JKP covers citizens only (PP 37/2021 art.2). A foreigner holding a KITAP is recorded as a foreign national.

rules.when: (person.employee.citizenship != "FOREIGNER" && (person.facts.JKP.since_months > 0 ? person.employee.age - person.facts.JKP.since_months / 12.0 : person.employee.age) < 54.0) && ((((base) - 0.0 > 0.0 ? (base) - 0.0 : 0.0)) > 0.0)

name: Pajak Penghasilan Pasal 21 (income tax withholding)
authority: PP 58/2023 and PMK 168/2023, in force 1 January 2024 — for every tax period but the last, a permanent employee's withholding is the monthly average effective rate (tarif efektif rata-rata, TER) for the employee's PTKP category applied to monthly gross. Category A is PTKP TK/0 (54,000,000) and TK/1 & K/0 (58,500,000), 44 brackets; category B is TK/2 & K/1 (63,000,000) and TK/3 & K/2 (67,500,000), 40 brackets; category C is K/3 (72,000,000), 41 brackets — all transcribed from the PMK 168/2023 Lampiran. Employee JHT (2%) and JP (1%) are charged as their own schemes and are not read as a relief on this scheme’s base: PMK 168/2023 art.15 applies the TER to gross. The last tax period is the first rung: the annual UU PPh art.17(1)(a) progression on PKP = year gross − biaya jabatan (5%, at most 6,000,000; PMK 250/PMK.03/2008) − the year's employee JP and JHT (PMK 168/2023 art.10(3)(b), iuran terkait program pensiun dan hari tua kepada BPJS Ketenagakerjaan) − PTKP, PKP rounded down to the whole thousand (UU PPh art.17(4)), less the year's withholding, a negative charge being the refund. Employer-borne JKK, JKM and the 4% Kesehatan are additions to the taxable gross (`produced.<code>.employer` in `assessed_on`). Applied 2026-09-18: employer-borne JKK, JKM and BPJS Kesehatan premiums are additions to the gross (PMK 168/2023 art.5(1)); in the five labour-intensive sectors an employee with a monthly gross up to 10,000,000 has the PPh 21 borne by the government for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods (PMK 10/2025, PMK 105/2025; entity fact `pph21_dtp_sector`), so nothing is withheld from them. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): UU 36/2008 art.7(1): the PTKP dependant count is the dependants in a direct line of blood or marriage and adopted children, at most three (`employee.dependents_count`, capped), not the children on record; the `ptkp` election KI is PMK 168/2023 art.9(3): a married woman who shows the local government's written statement that her husband has no income is given PTKP for herself, the married status and her dependants — never the spouse's own 54,000,000, which UU 36/2008 art.7(1) grants only in a combined annual return, not in withholding (corrected 2026-09-23); PMK 168/2023 art.10(2): biaya jabatan is 5% to Rp 500,000 a month, so the year’s cap is 500,000 for each month employed (`year.months_employed`); PMK 10/2025 art.2: the Government-borne PPh 21 is for a gross fixed and regular income of at most Rp 10,000,000 in the month (`BASE` and the fixed allowances), not the whole taxable base; PP 68/2009: severance (pesangon, UPMK) is taxed at its own final rates and is outside the TER base; a non-resident is under PPh 26. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): UU 36/2008 art.21(5a) as amended by UU 7/2021 (HPP): the withholding rate for a taxpayer without an NPWP is 20% higher than for one who shows it — every rung, the year-end reckoning included, is multiplied by 1.2 under the PPH21 election `no_tax_id`. Since UU KUP art.2(1a) as amended by UU 7/2021 a resident’s NIK serves as the NPWP and DJP PENG-6/PJ.09/2024 applies no surcharge where a valid NIK is given, so the election is for a recipient with neither. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 3): PMK 168/2023 art.9(4) — the PTKP (and so the TER category and the December reckoning) is the status at the start of the calendar year. The PPH21 elections `ptkp_marital_status`, `ptkp_dependants` and `ptkp` are dated declarations whose later changes apply from the next 1 January (`change_effect` YEAR_START); unrecorded, the employee's current marital status and dependants count are read. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): tax residence (UU PPh art.2(3)–(4)), the PTKP status and dependants at 1 January (art.7(2)), the tax identity (art.21(5a)) and, for a married employee, the gender are declared inputs; an unknown one stops the calculation rather than taking the resident, favourable or current-record reading.

rules.when: base > 0.0 && !(person.terms.tax_residency in ["RESIDENT", "NON_RESIDENT"])
rules.refusal: Record tax residency as resident or non-resident on the employment terms before calculating Indonesian withholding: UU PPh art.2(3)–(4) makes an individual resident by residence, 183 days’ presence in twelve months, or presence with intent to reside, and sets no default for an unknown one (PPh 21 against PPh 26).

rules.when: base > 0.0 && person.terms.tax_residency == "RESIDENT" && !("ptkp_marital_status" in scheme.election_keys && "ptkp_dependants" in scheme.election_keys && "no_tax_id" in scheme.election_keys)
rules.warning: PTKP status or dependants on 1 January, or whether the employee holds an NPWP or NIK, not declared: the employee declares them (UU PPh art.7(2), art.21(5a); PMK 168/2023 art.9(4)) and no status can be assumed, so this payroll withheld no PPh 21. Record the declaration; the December calculation then settles the year’s tax on it.

elections.label: PTKP tax status
elections.description: PMK 168/2023 art.9(3): `KI` where a married woman employee shows the local government’s written statement that her husband has no income, so her PTKP includes the spouse and dependants. Unrecorded is no such statement: a married woman’s PTKP is her own.

elections.label: PTKP marital status on 1 January
elections.description: UU PPh art.7(2); PMK 168/2023 art.9(4): the PTKP is the status at the start of the calendar year (for a person arriving to reside in Indonesia, the start of the arrival month). A later change applies from the next 1 January. A resident employee’s status is declared, never read from the current family record.

elections.label: PTKP dependants on 1 January
elections.description: UU PPh art.7(1)(c), (2): family by blood or marriage in a direct line and adopted children, wholly supported, at most three, counted at the start of the year. Declared by the employee; the household record does not establish it.

elections.label: No NPWP and no NIK usable as NPWP
elections.description: UU PPh art.21(5a): an employee without an NPWP is withheld at a rate 20% higher. A resident’s NIK serves as the NPWP once validated (UU KUP art.2(1a) as amended by UU 7/2021; PMK 112/2022; DJP PENG-6/PJ.09/2024), so the surcharge applies only where neither is held. Declared for every resident employee; there is no default.

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Hari Tua (old-age savings)
authority: PP 46/2015 art.16 — 5.7% of the monthly wage, 2% from the employee and 3.7% from the employer. SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AO5` = 2% (employee) and `!AR5` = 3.7% (employer); `!AE5` prints the combined 5.7%. NO CEILING: the highest-paid local employee, basic 22,380,750, is charged `AO17` 447,615 = 2% of the FULL wage, and the one foreign employee at 62,000,000 is charged `AK6` 1,240,000 = 2% of the full wage. Both would be clamped if any ceiling applied, and neither is. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): PP 46/2015 art.17(3): wages paid by the day make a month of the day’s wage × 25, whatever days were paid (`person.terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY"`).

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Pensiun (pension)
authority: PP 45/2015 art.28 — 3% of the monthly wage, 1% from the employee and 2% from the employer, charged on wage up to an annually adjusted ceiling (art.29). The ceiling is 11,086,300 from 1 March 2026 (SE BPJS Ketenagakerjaan No. B/1226/022026 of 25 February 2026, the art.29(3) uplift by 2025 GDP growth of 5.11%). SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AN5` = 1% (employee) and `!AQ5` = 2% (employer); `!AF5` prints the combined 3%. The ceiling and its March step are read off the one employee it binds — see ID_BPJS_CEILINGS_OBSERVED. JP covers Indonesian nationals only (the rule `when`). The one foreign employee is charged 0 in both `AJ6` and `AM6` on every (FOREIGN) sheet while still paying JHT, JKK, JKM and Kesehatan. Nationality is not a `rate_selector` axis; it belongs on employment_statutory_facts — see ID_JP_FOREIGN_EXCLUSION. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Applied 2026-09-23: PP 45/2015 art.15(1)–(3): the pension age is 56, 57 from 1 January 2019 and one year more every three years — 59 from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027; art.15(4): a participant who is still employed may choose to take the pension when work stops, at most three years after pension age. Contributions stop at 59 unless that choice is recorded (`scheme.elections.continue_after_pension_age`, to 62).

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Kecelakaan Kerja (work accident)
authority: PP 44/2015 Pasal 16(1): JKK by risk group — I 0.24%, II 0.54%, III 0.89%, IV 1.27%, V 1.74% of the wage, employer-borne. PP 37/2021 Pasal 11 as amended by PP 6/2025 funds JKP by recomposing 0.14% out of this rate; the employer is billed the full JKK rate and no separate JKP line (BPJS Ketenagakerjaan billing, and the seeded company's own listing). PP 44/2015 art.16(1) — an employer-only premium banded by the employer's registered work-risk group, in five groups from sangat rendah to sangat tinggi. PP 49/2023 art.16A, in force 6 October 2023, recomposes every rate by 0.14 percentage points into JKP for a wage earner required and registered in the JKP programme, giving 0.10 / 0.40 / 0.75 / 1.13 / 1.60; the art.16(1) rates 0.24 / 0.54 / 0.89 / 1.27 / 1.74 survive only for the art.16A(3) population, which this version does not model. SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AS5` = 0.89% and `!AC5` = 0.24% — the art.16(1) rates for class III (sedang) and class I (sangat rendah). The actuals follow 0.89% — Sutoyo `AS8` 65,670 = 0.89% x 7,378,688 exactly, and the foreign employee `AO6` 551,800 = 0.89% x 62,000,000 exactly, at two wages three orders of magnitude apart — so the workbook's risk group is class III, not the class IV the company record states. See ID_JKK_RISK_CLASS_CONFLICT. NO CEILING: the premium is charged on the full 22,380,750 and on the full 62,000,000. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): PP 44/2015 art.19(3): wages paid by the day make a month of the day’s wage × 25, whatever days were paid (`person.terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY"`).

name: Pajak Penghasilan Pasal 21 (income tax withholding)
authority: PP 58/2023 and PMK 168/2023, in force 1 January 2024 — for every tax period but the last, a permanent employee's withholding is the monthly average effective rate (tarif efektif rata-rata, TER) for the employee's PTKP category applied to monthly gross. Category A is PTKP TK/0 (54,000,000) and TK/1 & K/0 (58,500,000), 44 brackets; category B is TK/2 & K/1 (63,000,000) and TK/3 & K/2 (67,500,000), 40 brackets; category C is K/3 (72,000,000), 41 brackets — all transcribed from the PMK 168/2023 Lampiran. Employee JHT (2%) and JP (1%) are charged as their own schemes and are not read as a relief on this scheme’s base: PMK 168/2023 art.15 applies the TER to gross. The last tax period is the first rung: the annual UU PPh art.17(1)(a) progression on PKP = year gross − biaya jabatan (5%, at most 6,000,000; PMK 250/PMK.03/2008) − the year's employee JP and JHT (PMK 168/2023 art.10(3)(b), iuran terkait program pensiun dan hari tua kepada BPJS Ketenagakerjaan) − PTKP, PKP rounded down to the whole thousand (UU PPh art.17(4)), less the year's withholding, a negative charge being the refund. Employer-borne JKK, JKM and the 4% Kesehatan are additions to the taxable gross (`produced.<code>.employer` in `assessed_on`). Applied 2026-09-18: employer-borne JKK, JKM and BPJS Kesehatan premiums are additions to the gross (PMK 168/2023 art.5(1)); in the five labour-intensive sectors an employee with a monthly gross up to 10,000,000 has the PPh 21 borne by the government for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods (PMK 10/2025, PMK 105/2025; entity fact `pph21_dtp_sector`), so nothing is withheld from them. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): UU 36/2008 art.7(1): the PTKP dependant count is the dependants in a direct line of blood or marriage and adopted children, at most three (`employee.dependents_count`, capped), not the children on record; the `ptkp` election KI is PMK 168/2023 art.9(3): a married woman who shows the local government's written statement that her husband has no income is given PTKP for herself, the married status and her dependants — never the spouse's own 54,000,000, which UU 36/2008 art.7(1) grants only in a combined annual return, not in withholding (corrected 2026-09-23); PMK 168/2023 art.10(2): biaya jabatan is 5% to Rp 500,000 a month, so the year’s cap is 500,000 for each month employed (`year.months_employed`); PMK 10/2025 art.2: the Government-borne PPh 21 is for a gross fixed and regular income of at most Rp 10,000,000 in the month (`BASE` and the fixed allowances), not the whole taxable base; PP 68/2009: severance (pesangon, UPMK) is taxed at its own final rates and is outside the TER base; a non-resident is under PPh 26. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): UU 36/2008 art.21(5a) as amended by UU 7/2021 (HPP): the withholding rate for a taxpayer without an NPWP is 20% higher than for one who shows it — every rung, the year-end reckoning included, is multiplied by 1.2 under the PPH21 election `no_tax_id`. Since UU KUP art.2(1a) as amended by UU 7/2021 a resident’s NIK serves as the NPWP and DJP PENG-6/PJ.09/2024 applies no surcharge where a valid NIK is given, so the election is for a recipient with neither. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 3): PMK 168/2023 art.9(4) — the PTKP (and so the TER category and the December reckoning) is the status at the start of the calendar year. The PPH21 elections `ptkp_marital_status`, `ptkp_dependants` and `ptkp` are dated declarations whose later changes apply from the next 1 January (`change_effect` YEAR_START); unrecorded, the employee's current marital status and dependants count are read. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): tax residence (UU PPh art.2(3)–(4)), the PTKP status and dependants at 1 January (art.7(2)), the tax identity (art.21(5a)) and, for a married employee, the gender are declared inputs; an unknown one stops the calculation rather than taking the resident, favourable or current-record reading.

assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE + produced.JKK.employer + produced.JKM.employer + produced.KESEHATAN.employer

elections.label: PTKP tax status
elections.description: PMK 168/2023 art.9(3): `KI` where a married woman employee shows the local government’s written statement that her husband has no income, so her PTKP includes the spouse and dependants. Unrecorded is no such statement: a married woman’s PTKP is her own.

elections.label: PTKP marital status on 1 January
elections.description: UU PPh art.7(2); PMK 168/2023 art.9(4): the PTKP is the status at the start of the calendar year (for a person arriving to reside in Indonesia, the start of the arrival month). A later change applies from the next 1 January. A resident employee’s status is declared, never read from the current family record.

elections.label: PTKP dependants on 1 January
elections.description: UU PPh art.7(1)(c), (2): family by blood or marriage in a direct line and adopted children, wholly supported, at most three, counted at the start of the year. Declared by the employee; the household record does not establish it.

elections.label: No NPWP and no NIK usable as NPWP
elections.description: UU PPh art.21(5a): an employee without an NPWP is withheld at a rate 20% higher. A resident’s NIK serves as the NPWP once validated (UU KUP art.2(1a) as amended by UU 7/2021; PMK 112/2022; DJP PENG-6/PJ.09/2024), so the surcharge applies only where neither is held. Declared for every resident employee; there is no default.

name: PPh 21 final atas uang pesangon

rules.when: base > 0.0 && !(person.terms.tax_residency in ["RESIDENT", "NON_RESIDENT"])
rules.refusal: Record tax residency as resident or non-resident on the employment terms before calculating Indonesian withholding: UU PPh art.2(3)–(4) makes an individual resident by residence, 183 days’ presence in twelve months, or presence with intent to reside, and sets no default for an unknown one (PPh 21 against PPh 26).

rules.when: person.terms.tax_residency != "NON_RESIDENT" && base > 0.0

authority: PP 68/2009 art.2–4: severance pay (uang pesangon, uang penghargaan masa kerja) paid at once is subject to a final PPh 21 — 0% to Rp 50,000,000, 5% to 100,000,000, 15% to 500,000,000, 25% above — separately from the monthly TER withholding; the tiers accumulate over payments within two years, which this row reads as one payment. Applied 2026-09-23: PP 68/2009 art.1 angka 4 defines uang pesangon as income paid, under whatever name and in whatever form, in connection with the end of service or termination, including UPMK and UPH; uang pisah is paid only on termination (PP 35/2021 arts.50–54), so it is in this final base and outside the TER. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): uang kompensasi PKWT is paid when the fixed-term agreement ends (PP 35/2021 art.15(2)), in connection with the end of service, so it is in this final base too.

name: PPh 26 (non-resident withholding)
assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE + produced.JKK.employer + produced.JKM.employer + produced.KESEHATAN.employer

rules.when: person.terms.tax_residency == "NON_RESIDENT" && base > 0.0

authority: UU 36/2008 art.26(1)(d): remuneration for work paid to a non-resident individual (present under 183 days in twelve months, art.2(4)) is withheld at 20% of the gross amount, final, subject to a tax treaty; PPh 21 does not apply (`terms.tax_residency == "NON_RESIDENT"`).

name: PPh 21 final atas uang pesangon

rules.when: base > 0.0 && !(person.terms.tax_residency in ["RESIDENT", "NON_RESIDENT"])
rules.refusal: Record tax residency as resident or non-resident on the employment terms before calculating Indonesian withholding: UU PPh art.2(3)–(4) makes an individual resident by residence, 183 days’ presence in twelve months, or presence with intent to reside, and sets no default for an unknown one (PPh 21 against PPh 26).

rules.when: person.terms.tax_residency != "NON_RESIDENT" && base > 0.0

authority: PP 68/2009 art.2–4: severance pay (uang pesangon, uang penghargaan masa kerja) paid at once is subject to a final PPh 21 — 0% to Rp 50,000,000, 5% to 100,000,000, 15% to 500,000,000, 25% above — separately from the monthly TER withholding; the tiers accumulate over payments within two years, which this row reads as one payment. Applied 2026-09-23: PP 68/2009 art.1 angka 4 defines uang pesangon as income paid, under whatever name and in whatever form, in connection with the end of service or termination, including UPMK and UPH; uang pisah is paid only on termination (PP 35/2021 arts.50–54), so it is in this final base and outside the TER. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): uang kompensasi PKWT is paid when the fixed-term agreement ends (PP 35/2021 art.15(2)), in connection with the end of service, so it is in this final base too.

name: PPh 26 (non-resident withholding)
assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE + produced.JKK.employer + produced.JKM.employer + produced.KESEHATAN.employer

rules.when: person.terms.tax_residency == "NON_RESIDENT" && base > 0.0

authority: UU 36/2008 art.26(1)(d): remuneration for work paid to a non-resident individual (present under 183 days in twelve months, art.2(4)) is withheld at 20% of the gross amount, final, subject to a tax treaty; PPh 21 does not apply (`terms.tax_residency == "NON_RESIDENT"`).
